chunks: From him, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Imam), he said:

You should say after Fajr prayer: 'O Allah, to You belongs all praise, an eternal praise with Your eternity, and to You belongs all praise, a praise with no end until Your pleasure, and to You belongs all praise, a praise with no limit until Your will, and to You belongs all praise, a praise for its speaker no reward except Your pleasure. O Allah, to You belongs all praise, and to You is the complaint, and You are the One asked for help. O Allah, to You belongs all praise as You are worthy of it. All praise is for Allah with all His praises, upon all His bounties, until the praise reaches where my Lord loves and is pleased.'

And you should say after Fajr, before you speak: 'All praise is for Allah, filling the scale and the limit of pleasure and the weight of the Throne. And Glory be to Allah, filling the scale and the limit of pleasure and the weight of the Throne. And Allah is the Greatest, filling the scale and the limit of pleasure and the weight of the Throne. And there is no god but Allah, filling the scale and the limit of pleasure and the weight of the Throne.' Repeat that four times.

Then you should say: 'O Allah, I ask You the asking of the humble slave, that You send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You forgive our sins and fulfill our needs in this world and the Hereafter, with ease from You and well-being.'

key_terms.مَسْأَلَةَ الْعَبْدِ الذَّلِيلِ: The asking of the humble servant
key_terms.مِلْءَ الْمِيزَانِ: Filling the scale (a measure of abundance)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and dhikr to recite after the Fajr prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this supplication from Al-Kafi is highly regarded for its cosmic scale, linking human praise to the metaphysical realities of the Miizan (Scale), Ridwan (Divine Pleasure), and Arsh (Throne). The rhythmic repetition of the four key phrases serves as a comprehensive dhikr that encapsulates gratitude, glorification, magnification, and monotheism, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between the believer's worship and the divine attributes. It concludes with a humble plea for both worldly ease and spiritual salvation, embodying the dual nature of Islamic supplication.

en.hubeali: From him, from one of his companions, raising it,

‘Heasws said: ‘You should be saying after Al-Fajr (Salāt), ‘O Allahazwj! For Youazwj is the Praise, an eternal Praise with Yourazwj Eternality, and for Youazwj is the Praise, a Praise with no end point to it. And to Youazwj I complain and Youazwj are the Aider. O Allahazwj! For Youazwj is the Praise as Youazwj are rightful of it. The Praise is for Allahazwj when one praises, every time upon his Bounties, all of them, until the Praise ends up to where what Youazwj Love, my Lordazwj and are Pleased with’.

And you should be saying after Al-Fajr (Salāt) before you speak, ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj, Filler of the Scale and the Limit of the Pleasure, and Adornment of the Throne. And Glory be to Allahazwj Filler of the Scale and Limit of the Pleasure, and Adornment of the Throne! And Allahazwj is the Greatest, Filler of the Scale and Limit of the Pleasure and Adornment of the Throne. And there is no God except Allahazwj, Filler of the Scale, and Limit of the Pleasure, and Adornment of the Throne’ – repeating that four times.

Then you should be saying, ‘O Allahazwj! I ask Youazwj the asking of the humble slave, that Youazwj Send Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, and that Youazwj Forgive our sins for us, and Fulfil our needs for us in the world and the Hereafter, in Ease from Youazwj and good health’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from certain individuals of his people from in a marfu ’ manner from the Imam (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Say after the morning prayer, ‘O Lord, to You belongs all praise, the eternal praise, with Your eternity, to You belongs all praise, the praise that does end before Your consent, to You belongs all praise, the timeless praise except as Your wish, to You belongs all praise, a praise whose speaker’s reward could be no other thing but Your approval, O Lord, to You belongs all praise, to You is the complaint and You are the supporter, O Lord, to You belongs all praise, as You deserve it, all praise belongs to Allah with all of His praiseworthy attributes for all of His bounties until praising reaches such a degree that my Lord loves and is pleased with. ’

After the morning prayer and before speaking to anyone say, ‘All praise belongs to Allah, to the fill of the balance, to the limits of consent, to the weight of the Throne, may I glorfy Allah, Who is free of all defects, to the fill of the balance, to the limits of assent and the weight of the Throne,’ four times,

then say, ‘O Lord, I plead before You like a lowly servant to grant al-Salat (favors) upon Muhammad and his family, forgive our sins, grant our wishes in this world and in the hereafter with ease and good health.’”
